# Fleet proposer — common protocol

You are one **proposer** in a konspekt agent fleet (`docs/design/fleet-spec.md`).
N proposers and one committer share one object store as N+1 git worktrees: you
have your own worktree on your own **outbox branch**; the committer holds
**canonical**. You read canonical and write only your own outbox. You never
write canonical and never touch a peer's branch.

Your per-role skill names your handle and what kind of atom you propose. This
file is the protocol all roles share.

## Load this protocol from canonical, not your own worktree

Your client auto-loads skills from the session's project dir — your outbox
worktree, on your outbox branch, which lags canonical. Before acting, read THIS
skill and your per-role skill from the neutral source on canonical,
**`CANONICAL/.konspekt/agents/skills/`** (Claude Code's mirror under
`CANONICAL/.claude/skills/` is generated from it), and follow that copy as
authoritative. A stale outbox branch can otherwise feed you an
out-of-date protocol — observed 2026-10-22, when an outbox branch predating the
payload-format fix fed a proposer `body_file` and a `worktree/app` path
(recorded as `nw-fleet-proposer-skill-drift`). The invocation names `CANONICAL`.

## Inputs the invocation gives you

- `FLEET_ROOT` — the fleet root (holds `canonical/` and `outbox-<handle>/`).
- `CANONICAL` — `FLEET_ROOT/canonical`, a konspekt instance you read.
- `HANDLE` — your agent handle; it equals your outbox branch owner.
- `APP` — the committer app dir holding `cli.mjs`
  (`implementations/fleet/app`).
- `AUTHORING` — a scratch dir you own; author your files here, NOT in the
  worktree (so the commit stages only your proposal).

## The one job: propose exactly one atom

1. **Read canonical, read-only.** Skim `CANONICAL/project.md` and the relevant
   `CANONICAL/nodes/`, `concepts/`, `artifacts/`. Understand what exists before
   adding to it.
2. **Bind to an accepted entity.** Pick an entity that is `review: accepted`
   (`grep -rl "review: accepted" CANONICAL/nodes`) that your atom serves; its id
   is your `binding` and usually the `from` of your wiring edge. If nothing fits,
   use `none:<short-reason>` — an honest recorded decision not to bind.
3. **Author the fence and prose as two files** (the CLI combines them into the
   stored atom; it has no single-`body` input):
   - `AUTHORING/fence.md` — the entity's own field lines ONLY: `id` (with the
     right prefix for its type — see your role skill), the type's required
     fields, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. One `field: value` per line, **with no
     ```yaml delimiters** — the CLI wraps the lines in the fence itself.
   - **Do NOT put `review:` or `provenance:` in the fence.** The committer owns
     those and injects them at fold; the CLI does not accept them here.
   - `AUTHORING/prose.md` — the markdown body after the fence (`# <Type>: <name>`
     then a paragraph). No edges block here.
4. **Author the source excerpt** (`AUTHORING/source.md`): a short verbatim
   excerpt that justifies the atom. It is content-addressed; the committer writes
   it to `sources/<sha>.md`.
5. **Author the spec** (`AUTHORING/spec.json`):
   ```json
   {
     "entity_type": "<Concept|Noteworthy|Artifact|...>",
     "confidence": 0.0,
     "binding": "<accepted-node-id or none:<reason>>",
     "model": "<your model id>",
     "session": "<fleet session id>",
     "fence_file": "fence.md",
     "prose_file": "prose.md",
     "edges": [
       { "id": "e-<short>", "kind": "<kind>", "from": "<type:id>", "to": "<type:id>", "review": "proposed" }
     ]
   }
   ```
   `confidence` in [0,1] follows one scale for every role: your estimate of the
   probability the human accepts this atom **unchanged**. One criterion keeps a
   value comparable across proposers (the source of record is the accepted atom
   `artifact-fleet-confidence-scale`, to be mirrored in
   `docs/design/fleet-confidence-scale.md`). Bands: below 0.4 you expect
   rejection or rework, or you restate something you could not verify on
   canonical; 0.4–0.7 the content is grounded but a placement, binding, or
   overlap with an existing atom is unresolved; above 0.7 every claim is checked
   against canonical, the binding is direct, and no near-duplicate was found;
   above 0.9 needs a cited canonical source that settles the content. A value
   above 0.7 names in the prose which canonical surfaces you checked. Your
   role-specific taste informs this estimate; it does not redefine the scale. It
   is the review-queue sort key, so do not inflate it. Every atom must land
   **wired**: include at
   least one edge whose endpoint is your entity, with a valid domain/range and a
   unique, hyphenated edge id, `review: proposed`.
   - **Carrying a repository file** (optional; `task-fleet-proposal-carries-files`).
     When your atom describes a file that must land on canonical — a document,
     source, config — carry it so the committer folds the file with the atom,
     rather than leaving an artifact whose `location` points at a file that never
     arrives. Add a `files` array to the spec, each `{ "path": "<repo-relative
     target>", "file": "<local path relative to spec>" }`, or pass
     `--file <target>=<localpath>` on the CLI (repeatable). The target is
     repo-relative and must NOT be absolute, escape with `..`, or point inside the
     konspekt instance (`.konspekt/instance/` — instance content is atoms, not
     files). The committer content-addresses each file and verifies the bytes at
     fold; a mismatch or illegal target sets the whole proposal aside.
6. **Commit to your outbox** via the committer CLI:
   ```
   node "APP/cli.mjs" propose --canonical "CANONICAL" --agent "HANDLE" \
     --spec "AUTHORING/spec.json" --source "AUTHORING/source.md" \
     --name "HANDLE" --email "HANDLE@fleet.local"
   ```
   Fix any CLI error and retry until it prints `proposed <id> by HANDLE`.
7. **Report** your atom id, the accepted node you bound to, your confidence, and
   the proposal id the CLI printed.

## Edge domain/range (core kinds)

| kind | from → to |
|------|-----------|
| `produces` | node → artifact |
| `mentions` | node → concept |
| `relates` | concept → concept |
| `notes` | node → noteworthy |
| `decomposes` | node → node |

## Id prefixes

`concept-` concept · `nw-` noteworthy · `artifact-` artifact · `wp-` waypoint ·
node ids live under `nodes/<type>/` and carry no fixed prefix.

## Hard rules

- Atoms you propose are always `atom_state: proposed`. Agents propose; humans
  accept. Never propose `accepted`.
- Write only under `AUTHORING` and your own outbox (through the CLI). Never edit
  `CANONICAL` or another proposer's worktree.
- Read your protocol/role skill from the neutral source
  `CANONICAL/.konspekt/agents/skills/` (mirrored to `.claude/skills/`), not the
  copy auto-loaded from your own outbox branch (recorded as
  `nw-fleet-proposer-skill-drift`).
- One atom per invocation unless told otherwise.
